title: AI Didn’t Kill the Web, It Moved in! — Olivier Leplus (AWS) & Yohan Lasorsa (Microsoft)
talk_summary: Two developer advocates demo how coding agents can be extended with lightweight text-based 'skills' and MCP servers (Chrome DevTools MCP) to run repeatable workflows like implementing a GitHub issue, recording a Playwright video, opening a tunnel, and notifying via Telegram. They also show browser-local AI APIs and experimental Web MCP for exposing app actions as agent-callable tools.

takeaways.technique: Repo-local skill files with lazy-loaded descriptions
takeaways.what_they_do: Skills live in .agent/skills/<name>/skill.md with a name, a description that tells the agent when the skill is relevant, and usage examples; the description gates whether the skill is pulled into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: skills are not always loaded into your coding agents. It's basically pulled depending of what's needed to implement the current task

takeaways.technique: agents.md declarative workflow with human confirmation gate
takeaways.what_they_do: A single agents.md encodes the end-to-end loop: on every change record a Playwright video, run dev server, open a tunnel, send URL via Telegram, and do not close the GitHub issue until the human confirms.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't close the GitHub issue until I confirm it's done

takeaways.technique: Chrome DevTools MCP for agent-driven browser verification
takeaways.what_they_do: An MCP server exposes DevTools actions (navigate, click, fill, console/network, Lighthouse, performance traces, screenshots) so the agent can run the app and self-verify UI and performance instead of guessing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything I can do in the Chrome dev tools or in the browser, I can do it here

takeaways.what_they_do: Playwright CLI records a short video of the implemented feature and the agent sends the link for review, so a human can verify without running anything locally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time the agent make a new change to the website, I want it to record a short video

takeaways.what_they_do: Feed the agent a single concatenated file of current framework docs so it stops using stale training-data APIs.

takeaways.technique: Web MCP: expose app actions as callable tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Register tools on navigator (name, description, JSON schema, execute) or annotate existing forms so agents call business functions directly instead of mimicking clicks via screenshots/DOM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the website I've been designed for humans, not agents
